themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: On safe, auditable agent execution all three models again proposed a single gateway or proxy holding the credentials and enforcing spend, rate and audience caps, and the same instinct shows up as one data exit gate in provable downstream consent and deletion and one shared pre-send check in cross-channel journey orchestration.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models start small: a fixed panel of buyer questions, a consented panel of real people, or a holdout they leave running forever, just to have something honest to grade against.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers build repeating prompt panels because model output drifts, identity resolution answers recruit consented device panels because no one knows who is really the same person, and cross-channel incrementality answers turn budget changes into permanent randomized tests.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, a dollar, or a piece of content leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records, expiring every list you send, or judging results only by outcomes you can see yourself.
themes.evidence: Provable downstream consent and deletion answers fall back on canary profiles and expiring audience lists because trained models cannot unlearn a person, and safe agent execution answers note that vendor APIs expose no rollback or agent identity to check against.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what one more message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement has budget attached.
themes.evidence: Governance of generative content answers all say implied meaning and context cannot be checked by software, the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions of customer a political fight, and journey orchestration answers say no one can price a conversion against fatigue.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work with only what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers build a fast declared-agent lane because agents profit by passing as human, identity resolution answers point to platforms that profit from fragmentation, and ad supply integrity answers note the parties measuring fraud often earn from the traffic.
